title: Cost every bar, price for profit, and sell with confidence
course_title: Soap Making for Small Business: Cold-Process Bars and Simple Liquid Soap

say: Cost every bar, price for profit, and sell with confidence.
This is the video for Module 4 of Soap Making for Small Business.
Many small makers price by guessing, or by copying the seller next door. Months later they discover they were working for free.

Use your own current market prices

say: Every bar has four layers of cost. Ingredients, packaging, overheads like gas, water and transport, and your own labour. If you do not pay yourself, the business is not really making money.

say: The fix is simple arithmetic on your phone calculator.

say: All the naira figures here are approximate examples. Prices change quickly, so always use your own current prices.

panel.heading: Stop working for free

Use your own current market prices

say: For example, Amaka in Lagos makes 10 bars from a 1,000 g oil batch. Let us cost it.
Her oils, caustic soda and fragrance come to about 6,000 naira.
Printed wraps and labels for 10 bars are about 2,000 naira.
Her share of gas, water, gloves and transport is about 1,000 naira.
So the batch costs about 9,000 naira before labour. That is 900 naira per bar.
She also spends 3 hours at 1,000 naira per hour, which adds 300 naira per bar. Her full cost is about 1,200 naira per bar. Any price below that loses money.
Now set the price. A simple formula: price equals full cost divided by 1 minus the margin you want.

panel.heading: From full cost to a fair price
items: Price = full cost / (1 minus your margin)
Check similar handmade bars near you

say: For a 40% margin on 1,200 naira, divide by 0.60. That gives 2,000 naira, and 800 naira profit per bar.

say: A shop buying wholesale at 20% off pays 1,600 naira. You still make 400.

say: Then check what similar handmade bars sell for near you. If the market will not pay, cut costs, not your profit.

say: Finally, your start-up equipment. With 30,000 naira of equipment and 800 naira profit per bar, you must sell about 38 bars to get it back.

say: And use your real reject rate. If some bars are rejected, the cost of each good bar goes up.

panel.rule: Never price below your full cost per bar.

say: Wrap only cured bars. Wrapping fresh soap traps moisture and causes sweating and spots. Paper wraps or kraft boxes let the soap breathe.

say: Take photos near a window in daylight, with no flash, on a plain background. Shoot the wrapped bar, the cut bar, and lather in hands. No filters that change the colour.

say: Before you release any soap, see the money in your own banking, Opay or Moniepoint app. Agree delivery fees first, and keep customer details private.

panel.heading: Protect yourself from payment scams
left: Check your own bank or Opay app
right: Trust an SMS alert or screenshot
Share your PIN or one-time code

say: Fake bank alerts and edited screenshots are common. Never send goods because of an SMS or a picture. And never share your PIN or one-time code with anyone, even someone claiming to be your bank.

say: Bars cure for 4 to 6 weeks, so soap you sell in month two must be made in month one.
For example, Ngozi in Enugu wants to sell 60 bars in her first 90 days.
In days 1 to 14 she makes two more batches of 10 bars, each with a batch record.
In days 15 to 30 she registers her business name, prints labels and confirms her cost at 1,200 naira a bar.
In days 31 to 60 her first batches are cured. She sells 25 bars through WhatsApp and her church group.
In days 61 to 90 she sells 35 more, including 10 at wholesale to a salon.
That is 116,000 naira in revenue, 72,000 in cost, and about 44,000 naira profit after paying herself.

panel.heading: Ngozi plans 60 bars in 90 days
panel.rule: Production runs ahead of sales by the curing time.

say: To remember. Cost all four layers, including your time. Divide by good bars, not perfect batches. Build your price from the cost up. Confirm every payment yourself. And plan production weeks ahead of sales.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Cost four layers, including your own labour
Full cost per bar = batch cost / good bars
Confirm payment in your own app first
Plan production ahead by the curing time
